title: Orsen and the Cipher
premise: When Ada Voss is called to a coastal drowning that shouldn't be possible, she recognizes the dead man's clothes as her own—stolen from her closet while she slept. The victim, a retired harbor clerk, turns out to be the last living witness to a thirty-year-old insurance fraud that drowned a fishing village and paid out Ada's firm a fortune. As Ada's photographic memory dredges up the original case files she catalogued years ago, she realizes the killer is someone inside her own company, silencing witnesses one tide at a time. Ada must choose between protecting her career and exposing the firm that made her—ending with her testifying outside the law's reach, handing the cipher of forged policies to the village's survivors and walking away from everything she belonged to.
about_author: Sebastian Pemberton is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent a decade inspecting wrecked vessels along the North Atlantic coast. He writes mysteries from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where the fog still dictates his working hours.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Ada Voss, POV. Called to a drowning at Greyharbor, Ada recognizes the dead man's sweater and coat as her own—stolen from her closet days earlier. The police treat it as coincidence; her memory refuses to. Emotional beat: cold dread as the case becomes personal before it has even begun.

chapters.title: A Memory of Paper
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Digging through the firm's archives, she recalls cataloguing a 1994 claim from Greyharbor—a fleet 'lost' in a storm that locals swore never happened. She finds the dead man, Elias Marsh, was the claim's original witness. Emotional beat: the thrill of a pattern forming, shadowed by guilt at what her firm may have buried.

chapters.title: The Village That Drowned
chapters.summary: Ada, POV, traveling to Greyharbor. The surviving villagers are hostile, half-convinced she's come to buy their silence like the firm did thirty years ago. An old fisherwoman, Maren, hints that Elias had been receiving anonymous payments for decades. Emotional beat: Ada's first taste of belonging to something she doesn't yet understand—and being rejected by it.

chapters.title: Alibis in Amber
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Reconstructing the 1994 timeline from memory, she finds the storm report was forged—signed by an adjuster who died conveniently soon after. Someone at the firm knew, and someone is still protecting it. Her apartment is searched while she's away. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; the past is not past.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The fisherwoman finally trusts Ada with the village's side: her brother skippered the 'lost' fleet and never came home. Elias saw the ships scuttled deliberately and was paid to forget. Emotional beat: grief surfacing after thirty years, and Maren's wary hope that Ada might be different.

chapters.title: The Cipher
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Among Elias's effects she finds a coded ledger—policy numbers cross-referenced with payoffs, the 'cipher' of the whole fraud. Deciphering it points to a current senior partner: the son of the 1994 adjuster, still laundering the firm's original sin. Emotional beat: vertigo as the conspiracy reaches the top of Ada's own world.

chapters.title: A Second Body
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The firm's retired archivist—the only other person who could read the cipher—is found drowned, wearing clothes from Maren's house. The killer is framing the village, and the police begin hunting Maren. Emotional beat: horror and urgency; the killer has escalated and Ada is running out of witnesses.

chapters.title: The Man in Her Closet
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Reviewing her building's forgotten visitor logs with her perfect recall, she identifies the killer's accomplice: a junior colleague who copied her keys. Confronted, he confesses to theft but not murder—and reveals the partner plans to destroy the cipher and silence Ada at the anniversary regatta, when the whole coast will be watching the water. Emotional beat: betrayal at the center of her professional family.

chapters.title: Anniversary Tide
chapters.summary: Ada, POV, climax. At the regatta, Ada baits the partner into a confession aboard his own boat, the ledger's cipher recited from memory, and he tries to put her overboard as the tide turns. Maren and the villagers, tipped off, close in with the coast guard; the partner is taken alive as the water gives up one of the scuttled fleet's hulls. Emotional beat: terror, defiance, and the raw relief of being believed.

chapters.title: Belonging to Greyharbor
chapters.summary: Ada, POV, resolution. She resigns, hands the evidence to prosecutors and the villagers, and refuses the firm's settlement offer. Maren offers her a room for as long as she needs it. Standing where the drowned fleet went down, Ada finally feels the village accept her. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging—the justice the law couldn't give, given anyway.
